# B2B Support

`customer_support.model.b2b` · model · parent `—`

> Supporting an organisation that bought from us. The defining structural fact is that the person in the ticket is almost never the person who signed the contract and almost never the person who renews it. A ticket therefore has two audiences — the requester, who wants their problem to stop, and the account, which is quietly scoring whether we are safe to keep. Entitlement is real, written down and checkable, so what may be promised is bounded before an agent opens their mouth. Volume is moderate and complexity is high: the questions are configuration-specific, which is why deflection rates that look normal in consumer support are unachievable here and chasing them wastes a year. The error an operator carries in from B2C is treating ticket closure as the unit of success. Closing an admin's ticket in nine minutes while the economic buyer hears nothing for a quarter is how an account with a clean support dashboard churns.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| requester | an administrator, developer or power user at the customer, rarely the buyer and never the signatory |
| typical_resolution_hours | 24 |
| volume_shape | moderate volume, high complexity, business-hours concentrated, spiky around the customer's own release and upgrade windows |
| staffing_model | tiered L1/L2/L3 with a named escalation owner per account tier |
| coverage | business hours in the customer's region, on-call for severity-1 |
| automation_level | moderate — macros and a knowledge base carry the repetitive third; the rest is configuration-specific and resists deflection |
| notes | The canonical capability set is closest to this motion, so this branch mostly emphasises rather than adds or removes. |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.entitlement`

Requires `plan`, `coverage_hours`, `expires_at`


> Entitlement is checked, never assumed, in every B2B branch. An agent who promises a four-hour response the contract does not carry has created a liability out of goodwill, and the customer will quote it back for the rest of the term.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.sla_target`

Requires `clock_state`


> Clock state is mandatory here because `waiting_on_customer` and `open` look identical on a board and mean opposite things about whether we are currently in breach.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.escalation`


> An escalation without a named receiving owner is a complaint. In B2B that named owner is frequently on the customer's side of the table too — their internal sponsor — and an escalation that only names ours is half-mapped.
